name: James I of Scotland
role: King of Scots (1406–1437; personal rule from 1424)
summary: James pursued stronger hereditary kingship through lawmaking, estate recovery and campaigns against powerful nobles. His Catholic religious policy combined institutional reform with assertion of royal authority over the church.

sources.title: James I (r. 1406–1437)

sources.title: James I of Scotland

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (to be merged). Themes searched: government (kingship, parliament, courts, local rule, rebellion), church-state, economy (customs, bullion, labour, poor relief, craft bodies), world (France, England, Roxburgh), liberty and means. Acts of parliament were counted only where the text names the king as ordaining, forbidding, putting the articles, or writing in his own name (the 1425 articles and the 1432 letter), and DNB reports that legislation was directed by the king. The Kingis Quair is a poem and states no political position. Not answered: Crawar/Resby heresy burnings (the sources credit the inquisitor and bishops, not the king, and heresy is not blasphemy or apostasy), tariffs (customs read as revenue), natural resources (crown mines, not foreign control), consent of the governed and separation of powers (anachronistic). The rps.ac.uk record pages and the Exchequer Rolls/Durham Register copy were not reachable. The Albany executions followed an assize and are not read as political violence. Wording of acts is from Thomson's 1814 edition in OCR text.
